newsitem.title: USA: Intel sees higher fourth quarter revenues.
newsitem.headline: Intel sees higher fourth quarter revenues.

text.p: Intel Corp., the world's largest semiconductor maker, said Wednesday it expected revenues and gross profit margins to be sharply higher in the fourth quarter due to strong demand for personal computer chips.

The maker of the popular Pentium and Pentium Pro microprocessors said fourth quarter sales were expected to be "significantly higher" than the $5.14 billion generated in the third quarter ended Sept. 30 and gross margins, a key indicator of profitability, should exceed the third quarter's suprisingly strong rate of 57 percent.

The news, released in late afternoon, sent Intel's stock soaring $1.125 to $120 a share in after-hours trading. Earlier, Intel shares rose $4.875 to $118.875 on Nasdaq amid a strong stock market rally.
Industry analysts said the upbeat outlook by Intel, widely regarded as a bellwether for the technology group, should send shares of personal computer makers higher on Thursday.

"PC stocks are going to zoom," said analyst David Wu of First Chicago Corp. "The fact that they released this thing only five weeks under the bell (into the fourth quarter) tells me business is booming" he said.

Wu and other analysts hiked their estimates of what Intel might earn for the quarter to $1.70 to $1.75 a share. Charles Boucher of UBS securities said he is revising his estimate to $1.80 to $1.85 a share.
That is nearly twice what Intel earned a year ago, when it reported net income of $867 million, or 98 cents a share, on revnues of $4.58 billion.

Intel provided the forecast one day after California voters defeated a ballot initiative that would have expanded federal securities laws by giving investors the right to sue companies and executives in state court.
Citing the ballot initiative as its reason, Intel last month suspended its practice of making any forward looking statements until the election.
Intel said it expected fourth quarter expenses to rise about 17 percent to 20 percent from the third quarter's $1.01 billion due to higher holiday advertising costs and co-marketing programs.
The company reduced its capital expenditure forecast for all of 1996 to less than $3.4 billion from a previous $3.6 billion due to delays in building new administration offices.
